title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Ten documented no-admission places and activities around Toledo for a low-key outing with friends.

cards.title: Browse the Toledo Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: 2445 Monroe St, Toledo
cards.notes: Meet in the Green Building lobby, then make a self-guided loop through the galleries currently open to the public.
cards.short_summary: A free indoor art stop with free visitor parking.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum states that general admission and parking are free for all visitors.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Toledo Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Open to the public during regular museum hours; some galleries are temporarily closed for renovation and special exhibitions may charge.

cards.title: Take a trail loop at Wildwood
cards.subtitle: 5100 W Central Ave, Toledo
cards.notes: Use the official trail map and keep to marked paths while walking through the preserve’s woods, prairie, and river corridor.
cards.short_summary: A 493-acre former estate with a network of walking trails.
cards.evidence_claim: Metroparks Toledo says its parks are open daily and admission is free; Wildwood’s page identifies its trail system.
cards.access_notes: Park hours are 7 a.m. until dark daily. Metroparks notes that programs and attractions may have separate fees.

cards.title: Walk Swan Creek’s overlooks
cards.subtitle: 4301 Airport Hwy, Toledo
cards.notes: Start from the Airport Highway entrance and follow marked trails toward the creek, scenic overlooks, and swinging bridge.
cards.short_summary: An urban preserve with trails, creek habitat, and wildlife-viewing features.
cards.evidence_claim: Metroparks Toledo lists Swan Creek Preserve as open daily and states Metroparks admission is free.
cards.source_title: Swan Creek Preserve Metropark | Metroparks Toledo
cards.access_notes: Open 7 a.m. until dark every day. Skip reservable facilities if you want to keep the outing free.

cards.title: See public art at Glass City
cards.subtitle: 1505 Front St, Toledo
cards.notes: Walk the riverfront and pause at Beacon Tower, the slag-ladle sculpture, Rain Towers, and Field of Histories.
cards.short_summary: A Maumee River park with documented public-art features.
cards.evidence_claim: Metroparks Toledo states admission is free and identifies public-art features at Glass City Metropark.
cards.access_notes: Most of the park is open 7 a.m. to dark; the Market Hall and Ribbon area has separate posted hours. Paid rentals and food are optional.

cards.title: Do the Middlegrounds trail scavenger hunt
cards.subtitle: 111 Ottawa St, Toledo
cards.notes: Bring a phone or use the posted information cards to follow the one-mile Technology Explorer route from Roundhouse Shelter.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided, geocaching-style activity beside the Maumee River.
cards.evidence_claim: Metroparks Toledo provides a self-guided Technology Explorer at Middlegrounds and states Metroparks admission is free.
cards.access_notes: The route is about one mile round trip and takes roughly 30–45 minutes. Stay on the trail and do not collect natural items.

cards.title: Stroll Toledo Botanical Garden
cards.subtitle: 5403 Elmer Dr, Toledo
cards.notes: Pick a garden path, walk at conversation pace, and use the grounds as a relaxed outdoor meetup instead of a ticketed attraction.
cards.short_summary: A named Metroparks garden destination for a no-cost walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Toledo Botanical Garden is a Metroparks Toledo destination, and Metroparks states that admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Metroparks are open 7 a.m. to dark daily. Do not bring dogs; Metroparks rules exclude dogs from Toledo Botanical Garden.

cards.title: Walk the woods at Secor
cards.subtitle: 10001 Central Ave, Berkey
cards.notes: Choose a marked hiking or all-purpose trail and set an easy turnaround point so the group can explore without needing gear or a reservation.
cards.short_summary: A nearby Metropark for a straightforward woodland walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Secor is a Metroparks Toledo park, and Metroparks states that admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Metroparks are open 7 a.m. to dark daily. Admission is free, while some programs, attractions, and reservations may have fees.

cards.title: Take a Pearson nature walk
cards.subtitle: 761 S Lallendorf Rd, Oregon
cards.notes: Use the park map to choose a marked route, then pause at the water and woodland areas for a quiet, phone-free group walk.
cards.short_summary: A Metropark day-use destination with walking trails and natural areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Pearson is a Metroparks Toledo park, and Metroparks states that admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Metroparks are open 7 a.m. to dark daily. Admission is free; avoid reservable facilities and paid programs for a no-cost visit.

cards.title: Rally at Ottawa Park Tennis Courts
cards.subtitle: Ottawa Park, Toledo
cards.notes: Bring your own racquets and balls, reserve a court if needed, and set up a casual doubles rotation for a social hour outdoors.
cards.short_summary: Four city tennis courts designated free for regular play.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Toledo says Ottawa Park’s four tennis courts are always free and may be reserved by residents for regular play.
cards.source_title: Ottawa and Jermain Parks | City of Toledo
cards.access_notes: Bring your own equipment. The city says residents may reserve courts for regular play or events.

cards.title: Ride the Ottawa-Jermain trail
cards.subtitle: Ottawa and Jermain Parks, Toledo
cards.notes: Bring a maintained bike and helmet, stay on the designated 6.4-mile route, and match pace to the least experienced rider in your group.
cards.short_summary: A named city mountain-bike trail with no playing fee.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Toledo describes the Ottawa-Jermain route as an always-free, 6.4-mile mountain bike trail.
cards.source_title: Ottawa and Jermain Parks | City of Toledo
cards.access_notes: The city lists the trail as always free. Ride within your ability, use appropriate safety gear, and follow posted trail conditions.
